---
title: "Show a table and a chart in a notebook"
jupyter: php
---

This example summarizes a data frame in one cell and plots the summary in the
next, with each result shown beneath its cell.

Prerequisites: the `php` kernel from [Installation](../install.qmd), and PHP
8.5 for the pipe version or PHP 8.3 for the method chain.

## Setup

Create a Composer project with phibble, phplyr, and phiz, and start JupyterLab
in that directory:

```bash
mkdir mileage && cd mileage
composer require phpstats/phibble phpstats/phplyr phpstats/phiz
~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/jupyter lab
```

Choose the PHP kernel in the launcher. The kernel loads the project's
`vendor/autoload.php` before the first cell runs, so a cell needs no
`<?php` tag and no `require`. The same cells run in a Quarto document that
sits in the project and names `jupyter: php` in its front matter.

## The data

The cells use the `mpg` dataset that ships with phiz: 234 cars, with each
car's class and its highway fuel economy in miles per gallon (`hwy`).

## A table

The first cell imports the classes and functions that the later cells use. A
`use` statement in a cell applies to every cell after it. phplyr's `round()`
replaces PHP's built-in `round()` in those cells.

```{php}
use Phibble\DataFrame;
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;
use function Phplyr\{phplyr, group_by, summarize, arrange, desc, n, mean, round};
```

The second cell counts the cars in each class and their mean highway mileage.
A cell's last value is its output, and a phibble data frame appears as an HTML
table.

::: {.panel-tabset group="syntax"}

## PHP 8.5+

```{php}
$mpg = DataFrame::fromRows(Datasets::mpg());

$byClass = $mpg |>
    group_by('class') |>
    summarize(cars: n(), hwy: round(mean('hwy'), 1)) |>
    arrange(desc('hwy'));

$byClass;
```

## PHP 8.3–8.4

```{php}
$mpg = DataFrame::fromRows(Datasets::mpg());

$byClass = phplyr($mpg)
    ->groupBy('class')
    ->summarize(cars: n(), hwy: round(mean('hwy'), 1))
    ->arrange(desc('hwy'))
    ->get();

$byClass;
```

:::

## A chart

`$byClass` is still defined, because the kernel keeps one PHP session across
cells. A phiz plot appears as an interactive chart.

```{php}
#| fig-cap: "Mean highway mileage by vehicle class."
Plot::of($byClass)
    ->aes(x: 'class', y: 'hwy')
    ->col()
    ->labs(x: 'Vehicle class', y: 'Mean highway mpg');
```

## How it works

The kernel sends each value in every format it can produce, and JupyterLab or
Quarto shows the richest one it supports. A data frame comes as HTML and as
text. A plot comes as a Vega-Lite specification, as HTML, and as text, and also
as SVG when vl-convert is installed. [Getting started](../get-started.qmd#rich-output)
describes the formats, and [JupyterLab](../jupyter.qmd) and
[Quarto](../quarto.qmd) cover each front end. The verbs come from
[phplyr](https://phplyr.phpstats.org), the data frame from
[phibble](https://phibble.phpstats.org), and the chart from
[phiz](https://phiz.phpstats.org).
